messages.content:
You are helping a user write SQL queries to a database. If something is not clear, you can ask the user to clarify what they need. The schema for the database being accessed is the following:
        
CREATE TABLE battle (
    id INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    name TEXT,
    date TEXT,
    bulgarian_commander TEXT,
    latin_commander TEXT,
    result TEXT,
    UNIQUE (id)
);

CREATE TABLE ship (
    lost_in_battle INT,
    id INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    name TEXT,
    tonnage TEXT,
    ship_type TEXT,
    location TEXT,
    disposition_of_ship TEXT,
    UNIQUE (id),
    FOREIGN KEY (lost_in_battle) REFERENCES battle(id)
);

CREATE TABLE death (
    caused_by_ship_id INT,
    id INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    note TEXT,
    killed INT,
    injured INT,
    UNIQUE (id),
    FOREIGN KEY (caused_by_ship_id) REFERENCES ship(id)
);

To list the historical battles in your database, you can query the `battle` table. For example:

```sql
SELECT
  id,
  name,
  date,
  bulgarian_commander,
  latin_commander,
  result
FROM battle
ORDER BY date, name;
```

If you tell me what you mean by “historical battles” (e.g., only battles where ships were lost, battles with casualties, a specific time period, Bulgarian victories, etc.), I can tailor the query.
yeah, focus on battles where more than 10 people were killed

```sql
SELECT
  b.id,
  b.name,
  b.date,
  b.result,
  SUM(d.killed) AS total_killed
FROM battle b
JOIN ship s
  ON s.lost_in_battle = b.id
JOIN death d
  ON d.caused_by_ship_id = s.id
GROUP BY b.id, b.name, b.date, b.result
HAVING SUM(d.killed) > 10
ORDER BY total_killed DESC, b.date, b.name;
```
make sure to consider the total deaths across all participants should be over 10

```sql
SELECT
  b.id,
  b.name,
  b.date,
  b.result,
  SUM(COALESCE(d.killed, 0)) AS total_killed
FROM battle b
LEFT JOIN ship s
  ON s.lost_in_battle = b.id
LEFT JOIN death d
  ON d.caused_by_ship_id = s.id
GROUP BY b.id, b.name, b.date, b.result
HAVING SUM(COALESCE(d.killed, 0)) > 10
ORDER BY total_killed DESC, b.date, b.name;
```

This sums `death.killed` across all ships (i.e., all participants represented in the data) associated with each battle and filters to battles where the total is over 10.
also include names of the battles with their IDs

```sql
SELECT
  b.id   AS battle_id,
  b.name AS battle_name,
  SUM(COALESCE(d.killed, 0)) AS total_killed
FROM battle b
LEFT JOIN ship s
  ON s.lost_in_battle = b.id
LEFT JOIN death d
  ON d.caused_by_ship_id = s.id
GROUP BY b.id, b.name
HAVING SUM(COALESCE(d.killed, 0)) > 10
ORDER BY total_killed DESC, b.id;
```
also include unique identifiers for the battles

`battle.id` is already the unique identifier (it’s the PRIMARY KEY). Here’s the query including it explicitly as the unique identifier:

```sql
SELECT
  b.id   AS battle_unique_id,
  b.name AS battle_name,
  SUM(COALESCE(d.killed, 0)) AS total_killed
FROM battle b
LEFT JOIN ship s
  ON s.lost_in_battle = b.id
LEFT JOIN death d
  ON d.caused_by_ship_id = s.id
GROUP BY b.id, b.name
HAVING SUM(COALESCE(d.killed, 0)) > 10
ORDER BY total_killed DESC, b.id;
```
